```{r sourcing, include = TRUE}
#source the R folder to load any packages and functions
lapply(dir('R', '*.R', full.names = TRUE), source)

#read in finalized data
dat <- readRDS("Output/Data/final_data.rds")

#subset for different analyses
food <- dat[food == 0 | food == 1]  #just food add and control grids

```



```{r basic linear mixed model using non-standardized variables, include = TRUE}

#build off the previous base model and incorporate random effects (same as delaney) and other covariates
mixmod <- lmer(growthrate ~ 
              littersize*treatment_food*cones_tree_prev +
              density +
              mother_age + 
              mother_age^2 +
              sex + 
              mast + 
              (1|mother_id/litter_id) +
              (1|year), 
            food)

#summaries
anova(mixmod)

#get effects table for model
mix_effs <- as.data.table(ggpredict(mixmod, terms = c("littersize", "cones_tree_prev", "treatment_food")))

ggplot(mix_effs)+
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = x, ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high, group = group, fill = group), alpha = 0.2)+
  geom_line(aes(y = predicted, x = x, color = group, group = group), linewidth = 1)+
  scale_color_discrete(name = "log(tree cones)")+
  scale_fill_discrete(name = "log(tree cones)")+
  labs(x = "Litter size", y = "Growth rate (g/day)", subtitle = "Food Treatment")+
  facet_wrap(~facet)+
  theme_bw()
  
```


```{r bivariate response model, include = TRUE}

#formula:
# growth rate-litter size ~ treatment_food*cones_tree_prev*density + mother_age + mother_age^2 + sex + mast + random effects

#using base R to get an idea of things but can't use random effects with cbind
biv_lm <- lm(cbind(littersize, growthrate) ~ treatment_food*cones_tree_prev*density + mother_age + mother_age^2 + sex + mast, data = food)

# 3. View the full summary
summary(biv_lm)

#get effects table for model
biv_lm_effs <- as.data.table(ggpredict(biv_lm, terms = c("density", "cones_tree_prev", "treatment_food")))

ggplot(mix_efoodggplot(mix_effs)+
```
